skill.name: codedna
skill.description: Generate a "DNA profile" of a codebase's coding and repository-prose style (naming, comments, docs, messages, structure, error handling, and idioms), then use it so new or AI-written contributions match the existing author. Use this skill when the user wants code or repository prose to blend in, mimic a coding style, capture house conventions, build a style guide from existing work, onboard to an unfamiliar repo's conventions, or check code, docs, or a diff for AI tells. Triggers on phrases like "match my coding style", "make it look like I wrote it", "codedna", "capture the conventions", "style guide from the code", "why does this read as AI-generated", "genetic map of the code", "mimic the codebase", and on significant contributions to an existing repo where matching house style matters. Do not use it for general writing with no repository or author corpus.
skill.summary: Document repository conventions and use them to write or review code and project prose.
skill.author: hannsxpeter

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are literal text, and the Python subprocess uses a fixed Git subcommand without a shell. The documented workflow can run unverified repository commands, read linked files outside scope, and persist generated content as agent guidance. Its authorship language also encourages reviewers to mistake style conformity for provenance.

remediation.suggestion: Review and obtain approval for repository-defined commands before running them. Disable external diff helpers and text conversion when reviewing untrusted Git repositories.

remediation.issue: Author filter substituted into shell text
remediation.suggestion: Pass the author filter as a literal argument rather than substituting user text into a shell command.

remediation.issue: Source reads can leave the selected directory
remediation.suggestion: Reject symlinked source files or verify that resolved paths stay under the approved root. Do not fall back to walking ignored paths without explicit approval.

remediation.issue: Unapproved or out-of-scope agent instruction updates
remediation.suggestion: Make wiring an explicit opt-in with a file preview. Reject symlinked files and parent directories that resolve outside the approved repository.

remediation.issue: Repository text can become persistent agent guidance
remediation.suggestion: Keep source excerpts separate from conventions and exclude embedded directives or sensitive text. Require human review of the profile and wiring diff before activation.

remediation.issue: Style conformity is presented as proof of authorship
remediation.suggestion: Report convention mismatches only. Preserve required disclosures and security checks, and do not infer authorship from style.

semantic_findings.title: Source File Reads Can Escape the Selected Scope
semantic_findings.description: Source selection accepts symlinked files and follows them when reading. Empty Git results also trigger a walk without Git ignore rules.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file check and open call follow symlinks without checking containment. An empty Git file list selects the generic directory walk.

semantic_findings.title: Profile Wiring Changes Agent Instructions by Default
semantic_findings.description: Mapping creates or updates persistent agent instructions without a separate approval step. The wiring helper follows symlinked destinations, so writes can leave the selected repository.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow requires default wiring and reports changes afterward. The helper reads and writes its destination paths without checking resolved containment.

semantic_findings.title: Repository Text Can Reach Future Agent Sessions
semantic_findings.description: The workflow copies source snippets into a profile that future agents are told to follow. Embedded directives in copied content could influence later sessions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions require real snippets and make the profile ongoing guidance without an explicit review step. No direct attempt to override this audit was found.

semantic_findings.title: Style Guidance Encourages Misleading Authorship Claims
semantic_findings.description: The workflow asks whether work would pass as the author's own and encourages removing signs of different authorship. This can mislead reviewers where disclosure is required.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The Match and Check criteria explicitly judge whether work appears to come from a particular author. Consistent style does not establish who wrote it.

content.value_statement: Repository conventions can be difficult to learn when they are spread across source files and documentation. CodeDNA records them in a profile for writing and reviewing changes.
actual_capabilities: Builds a CODEDNA.md profile from representative files and repository configuration.
Separates formatter and linter rules from conventions observed in source files.
Measures identifier lengths, function sizes, comment density, and selected error message patterns with a Python helper.
Uses a style profile and neighboring files to guide code and documentation changes.
Reviews files, pasted text, or Git diffs for convention mismatches and suggests revisions.
Can create or update repository instructions that direct coding agents to the style profile.
limitations: Measurements use language-specific heuristics and may omit large, minified, or unsampled files.
A style profile can become outdated after major changes to tooling or project conventions.
Style differences do not establish authorship or prove AI use.
A style review does not verify correctness or replace security and test review.

use_cases.title: Document Team Conventions
use_cases.description: Create a profile for a repository and show which conventions come from tools and which come from existing code.

use_cases.title: Prepare a First Contribution
use_cases.description: Compare nearby files to learn how the project names functions, writes tests, and presents errors.

use_cases.title: Review Documentation in a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Compare changed documentation with project examples and suggest revisions without making claims about who wrote it.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize Existing Conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize naming and comment conventions from an approved profile and two nearby files. Do not edit files.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Profile for One Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a style profile for the billing module from approved local files. Separate enforced rules from observed patterns. Do not run project commands or change agent instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Match Nearby Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the approved style profile and nearby tests to draft a test for the new validation rule. Preserve existing error handling and disclosure requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Change Across Code and Prose
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this diff with the approved profile. Group findings by naming, error handling, and documentation. Cite nearby evidence, suggest revisions, and flag any stale rules.

output_examples.input: Summarize conventions in the service module.
output: Enforced: The formatter sets indentation and line endings.
Observed: Boolean helpers use question-style names. Comments explain decisions rather than restating the code.
Exception: Older integration tests use longer names than unit tests.

output_examples.input: Check this staged change for consistency with repository prose.
output: Error messages: Nearby errors use short fragments without periods. Shorten the new validation message to name the invalid field.
Documentation: The new heading matches the surrounding guide. No change is needed.

best_practices: Limit profiling to a directory or language you are authorized to inspect.
Use representative examples, separate enforced rules, and refresh the profile after deliberate convention changes.
Review generated profiles and proposed agent instruction changes before enabling them.
anti_patterns: Treating style mismatches as evidence of AI use or a particular author.
Using generated files or third-party code as primary evidence for team conventions.
Running unverified repository scripts or copying sensitive examples into the profile.

faq.question: What does Map mode produce?
faq.answer: It produces a CODEDNA.md profile covering the selected repository scope. The default workflow also updates agent instruction files.

faq.question: Is Python required?
faq.answer: The bundled helpers require Python. The assistant can draft a profile from configuration and source files without collecting automated measurements.

faq.question: Can I focus on one part of a repository?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose a subdirectory or language, and use nearby files to account for local differences.

faq.question: What does Check mode review?
faq.answer: It compares a named file, pasted material, or Git diff with the style profile and suggests revisions for specific deviations.

faq.question: Does this replace a formatter or linter?
faq.answer: No. It records enforced settings and describes conventions that formatting and linting tools may not cover.

faq.question: Can it tell who wrote a change?
faq.answer: No. It can report style differences, but those differences do not establish authorship or whether AI was used.
